Former Legislative Council member Wong Kam-fai is charged with dangerous driving and other offences, and is on bail pending trial. He served as a member from December 2022 to July this year. "集誌社" reviewed Legislative Council records and found that during Wong Kam-fai's tenure of over 42 months, his office's total operating expenses exceeded HK$10 million, including over HK$1.5 million in consultancy fees. He successively appointed Chan Tak-ming, president of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association" which he founded, and the association's vice president Ng Hok-ling, as consultants. Chan Tak-ming has been continuously engaged since January 2023, receiving HK$20,000 to HK$30,000 per month, totalling over HK$1 million in consultancy fees. According to the guidelines for Legislative Council members' application for reimbursement of working expenses, "members should not engage as consultants their political parties or any organisation over which their political party has control." Is there any problem with hiring key members of related organisations as paid consultants? The Legislative Council Secretariat replied to "集誌社"'s enquiry stating that the guidelines have been listed and no further comment would be made. Wong Kam-fai, who has no political affiliation, responded by saying that the association operates on a voluntary, non-profit basis. In addition, towards the end of his first term, Wong Kam-fai also distributed bonuses to his office staff. In that month, he declared over HK$773,000 in total to the Legislative Council as staff expenses.

Over HK$10 million in office operating expenses during his term

"集誌社" reviewed Wong Kam-fai's "reimbursement of office operating expenses" in the Seventh Legislative Council, which ranged from approximately HK$2.877 million to HK$2.984 million per year. From October 2025, in the Eighth Legislative Council, the amount was raised to HK$3.02 million. During his 42-month tenure, Wong Kam-fai declared over HK$10 million in office operating expenses to the Legislative Council. In 2023 and 2024, his declared expenses were approximately HK$1.876 million and HK$2.89 million respectively.

However, in 2025, Wong Kam-fai's declared expenses were HK$4.006 million. The increase in expenses was due to factors including staff expenses rising from HK$2.24 million the previous year to HK$3.215 million, and consultancy fees increasing from HK$480,000 to HK$640,000. After Wong Kam-fai was re-elected in 2026, his expenses from January to June were HK$1.413 million.

Spent over HK$1 million hiring senior executives of his own association as legislative consultants

Reviewing the records, from February 2023 to June 2026, Wong Kam-fai declared over HK$1.5 million in consultancy fees to the Legislative Council. Of this, during the 36 months from 2023 to 2025, he continuously engaged Chan Tak-ming, president of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association," at HK$30,000 per month, spending HK$1.08 million. After Wong Kam-fai was re-elected in the current term until before his resignation, within six months, he continued to engage Chan Tak-ming at HK$20,000 per month, spending a total of HK$120,000. The "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association" was founded by Wong Kam-fai in 2016, and he serves as its executive president.

Three consultancy tenders, two bidders were "association" members

As early as March 2023, Wong Kam-fai submitted tender documents to the Legislative Council. At that time, the three consultancy tenders were from Tai Ching-fung, Chan Tak-ming, and Cheng Kwok-wai. Both Tai and Chan were members of the "Hong Kong Guangzhou Innovation and Technology Association," with Tai being the head of the finance group. Tai quoted HK$45,000, Cheng quoted HK$35,000, and Chan's quote was the lowest at HK$30,000; ultimately Chan secured the consultancy work.

The tender's scope of work stated that Chan's consultancy work involved assisting in advocating and planning innovation and technology, education, various social policies and issues; facilitating interactive communication across all sectors; and assisting in supporting various work of regional offices.

Engaged association vice president as consultant with only one quotation

Wong Kam-fai also engaged the association's vice president Ng Hok-ling as a consultant. From June 2023, Ng Hok-ling served as Wong Kam-fai's consultant on innovation and technology and education policy matters, receiving a consultancy fee of HK$5,000 in the first month, and subsequently HK$10,000 per month, totalling HK$315,000. There was only one quotation for Ng Hok-ling's consultancy work. Regarding the scope of work in the tender, Wong Kam-fai stated that Ng was "similarly well-versed in both innovation and technology and education policies," and could "respond quickly to work requirements, with flexible service arrangements, and his service quality meets the needs of my Council work."

Legislative Council guidelines: Should not engage political party-controlled organisations as consultants

According to Article 24 of the Legislative Council's "Guidelines for Members' Application for Reimbursement of Working Expenses," "a Member should not engage as a consultant any company/organisation in which his/her political party has a financial interest or control." Wong Kam-fai, who has no political affiliation: Association operates on a non-profit basis

"集誌社" enquired with Wong Kam-fai whether engaging key members of related organisations as consultants might conflict with the guidelines. Wong Kam-fai replied that Chan Tak-ming's role covered district and political liaison, while Ng Hok-ling covered the education sector. Wong Kam-fai said the association was founded by a group of like-minded innovation and technology professionals hoping to contribute to the development of innovation and technology in Hong Kong and the Mainland, "everyone works on a voluntary basis, and it has always operated in a non-profit manner." Reviewing the information, Wong Kam-fai has no political affiliation.

Office director received HK$276,000 upon contract completion

In addition to consultancy expenses, regarding the salary expenses of legislative assistants, reviewing the records, when Wong Kam-fai completed his term in 2025, he declared two staff expense items totalling over HK$773,000 to the Legislative Council, of which approximately HK$423,000 was for paid leave, together with salaries for November and December.

Wong Kam-fai also distributed approximately HK$350,000 in bonuses to five office staff. Among them, Wong Kam-fai's office director had a monthly salary of HK$63,500. Upon completion of her term in December, she received paid annual leave compensation, together with approximately HK$181,000 covering two months' salary, plus a bonus equivalent to 1.5 months' salary of HK$95,200, totalling HK$276,000. The other four staff members each received bonuses from Wong Kam-fai equivalent to 2.5 months' salary, ranging from HK$54,000 to HK$75,000.

Legislative Council Secretariat: Working expense reimbursement guidelines have been listed

"集誌社" had previously enquired with the Legislative Council Secretariat whether Wong Kam-fai's practices of hiring his own association's president and vice president as long-term consultants and distributing bonuses were appropriate. The Secretariat replied that the relevant details had already been listed in the guidelines for Legislative Council members' application for reimbursement of working expenses, and no further comment would be made.

Guiding principles of the "Guidelines for Legislative Council Members' Application for Reimbursement of Working Expenses" (partial) ・Members or their relatives should not have any direct or indirect financial interest in transactions involving applications for reimbursement. ・Members should avoid applying for reimbursement for any transaction that would lead the public to believe that the member, their relatives or business partners could benefit therefrom. ・Members should adhere to the principles of openness, fairness and accountability when using public funds. ・Where conflicts of interest cannot be avoided or have arisen, members should declare their interests when applying for reimbursement, and the declarations will be available for public inspection. ・If a transaction for which reimbursement is or may be applied for gives rise to a suspicion of conflict of interest... members should handle such matters in accordance with the principle of prioritising the public interest. ・Members should, as far as possible, separate their private affairs from those of the Legislative Council, and inform the public that they have done so in performing their duties, so as to avoid giving rise to any suspicion of conflict of interest or improper personal gain.

Guidelines for Legislative Council Members' Use of Consultancy Services: Members may engage consultants on a standing or non-standing basis... To avoid conflicts of interest, the following requirements must be met: ・Individual contracts should be signed with each consultant engaged. ・Contracts should clearly specify the scope of services to be provided by the consultant. ・The names of consultants and the fees charged should be listed on reimbursement application documents for public inspection. ・A copy of the contract should be submitted to the Secretariat (contracts need not be available for public inspection). ・Members or their relatives should not have any interest relationship with the engaged consultants. ・Members should not engage as consultants any company/organisation in which their political party has a financial interest or control.

In his declaration records, Wong Kam-fai labelled the bonus amount as "others," stating that no bonuses had been distributed in the first three years of his term, and that the arrangement was discretionary, "therefore not specified in the contract." He also stated that the team had assisted in driving and implementing various bills, motions and initiatives, and that "after prudent consideration of the office's financial position, a decision has been made to award the following staff members bonuses in recognition of their hard work and contributions during the Seventh Legislative Council term." Reviewing the "Guidelines for Application for Reimbursement of Working Expenses," members may set aside funds from their office operating expense reimbursements to pay staff contractual bonuses, double pay, or end-of-contract gratuities, etc. The amount of reserved funds should be determined according to the contracts signed by both parties and other legal obligations, and should not be excessive; members may receive the funds without having to submit supporting documents.

On 29 June this year, Wong Kam-fai was arrested by police on four charges including suspected drink driving and careless driving, after allegedly hitting two vehicles on the CUHK campus and leaving the scene. After the media exposed the case on 1 July without Wong Kam-fai having declared it to the Legislative Council, he attended the Reunification Day reception as usual for photo-taking, until 3 July, when Wong Kam-fai resigned from all his Legislative Council positions.

Apart from being a member of the Legislative Council's Election Committee constituency, Wong Kam-fai is also a member of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and Associate Dean (External Affairs) of CUHK's Faculty of Engineering. Following the drink driving incident, CUHK announced the suspension of his administrative duties to date. In September this year, police formally charged him with four offences including "dangerous driving," and he was granted bail, with the case adjourned to 11 November for further mention.
